system_description.narrative_title: Nvidia CEO spy-affair sparks systemic shock to the AI‑chip ecosystem
system_description.narrative_summary: The dominant narrative is that Jensen Huang’s alleged affair with a woman tied to Chinese intelligence has cascaded from a personal scandal into a corporate‑governance crisis, a market valuation shock, and intensified US national‑security and export‑control scrutiny of AI chips. As an open system this ties together processes (governance failure, security investigations, export policy formulation, market repricing, lobbying) with concrete actors (Nvidia, Huang, the board, US Congress/DOJ/Commerce, Chinese institutions, competitors, investors) and dated events (board meetings, probes, subpoenas, resignations, APEC/legislative actions). The story’s feedbacks — regulatory action feeding supply‑chain disruption and market volatility, and vice versa — make outcomes endogenous and highly path dependent.
system_description.scope: Within the system boundary: the AI‑chip industry centered on Nvidia; corporate governance and succession dynamics at Nvidia; US political and regulatory responses (Congress, DOJ, Commerce); global financial markets and investor flows reacting to disclosure and leadership events; China‑linked intelligence and industrial actors; downstream customers and competitors (cloud providers, automakers, AMD, Broadcom); supply‑chain nodes (Taiwan, Singapore, foundries). Included variables: board decisions, investigations/probes, export controls, lobbying, stock price/market cap moves, supply allocation, and diplomatic events tied to APEC/US‑China relations.
system_description.super_system: The global geopolitical‑economic system of US‑China strategic competition and the international technology/industrial ecosystem that underpins the AI boom.
adjacent_subsystems: Global financial markets and institutional investors
US national security and regulatory institutions (Congress, DOJ, Commerce)
China industrial policy, intelligence acquisition mechanisms, and state firms
Global semiconductor supply chain and manufacturing hubs (Taiwan, Singapore, foundries)

variables.name: Corporate governance robustness
variables.description: Measures the resilience, independence and effectiveness of corporate oversight structures and decision‑making processes within leading AI‑chip firms.

variables.name: Executive succession preparedness
variables.description: Measures the readiness, clarity and depth of planned leadership transitions and bench strength for top executive roles in major sector firms.

variables.name: Regulatory scrutiny intensity
variables.description: Measures the frequency, scope and severity of oversight actions, inquiries and enforcement activity directed at the AI‑chip sector by regulatory actors.

variables.name: Export‑control restrictiveness
variables.description: Measures the severity, breadth and operational impact of trade and export restrictions applied to advanced semiconductor technologies.

variables.name: Investor sentiment toward AI‑chip sector
variables.description: Measures prevailing investor optimism, risk tolerance and expectations about future earnings and growth in AI‑accelerator producers.

variables.name: Market valuation of key firms
variables.description: Measures aggregate market capitalisation and price level metrics for the principal firms that supply AI accelerators and related hardware.

variables.name: Market volatility
variables.description: Measures short‑term amplitude of price movements and uncertainty in financial markets relevant to the AI‑chip ecosystem.

variables.name: Supply‑chain allocation pressure
variables.description: Measures tightness, lead‑time stress and risk of allocation disputes across fabrication, packaging and logistics nodes that service AI‑chip demand.

variables.name: Downstream customer concentration
variables.description: Measures the degree to which sector demand is concentrated in a small number of large cloud, enterprise or vertical customers.

variables.name: Competitor scaling capacity
variables.description: Measures rival firms' ability to increase production, R&D and commercial capacity to absorb displaced demand or market share shifts.

variables.name: Lobbying intensity
variables.description: Measures the volume, frequency and aggressiveness of sectoral efforts to influence policy, legislation and regulatory decisions.

variables.name: Legal and investigatory activity
variables.description: Measures the rate and intensity of formal probes, subpoenas, internal investigations and litigation affecting firms and executives in the sector.

variables.name: Intelligence infiltration risk
variables.description: Measures the probability and prevalence of covert influence, information exfiltration or agent access within firms, projects or supply chains.

variables.name: Diplomatic tension
variables.description: Measures the intensity of cross‑border political frictions and state‑level diplomatic actions that affect technology cooperation and trade relations.

variables.name: Regulatory policy change rate
variables.description: Measures the speed and frequency at which laws, export rules and regulatory frameworks relevant to semiconductor trade are modified.

variables.name: Technological dependency concentration
variables.description: Measures the degree to which critical AI capabilities, architectures or supply inputs are concentrated in a single technology type or small number of providers.

catalysts.title: Congressional hearings on Nvidia-China ties
catalysts.description: Lawmakers pursue testimony and subpoenas about the CEO affair, chip exports and diversion risks; multiple hearings expected.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: lawmakers summon Huang, subpoenas floated, Democrats/Dems seek oversight and export limits.

catalysts.title: Wachtell/Joon Kim internal probe and board actions
catalysts.description: The external internal investigation will produce findings and board recommendations that could trigger governance changes or litigation.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Nvidia hires Wachtell and ex-prosecutor Joon Kim to lead probe; board investigation underway.

catalysts.title: Legislative push to tighten AI‑chip exports to China
catalysts.description: Bipartisan momentum and speaker comments signal efforts to draft/tighten export restrictions on AI accelerators tied to the scandal.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Speaker consensus forming, lawmakers push chip rules, calls to tighten China access after spy allegations.

catalysts.title: Commerce Dept decision on Megaspeed listing/controls
catalysts.description: A formal decision on Megaspeed's blacklist status or restrictions is likely, affecting customer access to U.S. chips.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Commerce delayed Megaspeed blacklist inclusion; Megaspeed says it cooperated with inspections.

catalysts.title: Board search and appointment of Nvidia permanent CEO
catalysts.description: Board search for a permanent CEO accelerates; an appointment or shortlist expected, clarifying leadership and direction.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Interim CEO named, many candidates discussed; board must craft job description and pick replacement.

catalysts.title: Escalation of export enforcement inspections and audits
catalysts.description: DOJ/Commerce/FBI increase audits and shipment inspections across customers and supply chains after diversion concerns.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: FBI/DOJ involvement noted; Megaspeed inspections mentioned and calls for preserving export records.

catalysts.title: Rivals and Chinese firms scramble for chip capacity
catalysts.description: Competitors and Chinese customers rush to secure alternative chip allocations and capacity, reshaping supplier bookings.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: Chinese AI firms rush to secure Nvidia capacity; analysts suggest AMD/Broadcom could win market share.

catalysts.title: APEC summit diplomatic flashpoints (Nov 16–18)
catalysts.description: Leaders meet Nov 16–18; the Nvidia scandal may surface in high-level talks, shaping immediate tech diplomacy signals.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: APEC summit Nov 16–18 mentioned; Huang's participation in doubt and China/US tech ties in focus.
